prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of the time-reversal-invariant topological insulator and the quantum spin Hall effect, and for the first experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall state in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: I keep B004 as my preferred configuration, unchanged from round 1. Having read all eight statements and the questions put in my own chair summary, the physics case has not weakened. Kane and Mele showed that time-reversal symmetry with spin-orbit coupling gives a Z2 invariant and protected helical edge states without a magnetic field; Molenkamp's group then measured the predicted edge conduction in HgTe quantum wells, in a device where the quantised conductance could have failed. That is a falsifiable prediction that survived, and about two decades of transport and ARPES work have left the interpretation stable. All eight members ranked B004 at opening and no one in round 1 argues against its scientific standing; even those who prefer another candidate name it as a first or second alternative. The three credited names map onto a coherent theory-plus-experiment prize. My answer to the chair's question on B004 is that a citation confined to the two-dimensional quantum spin Hall effect and its first observation is defensible: it claims neither the three-dimensional topological insulator programme nor the 2016 topological phase transition work, and it answers the overlap concern as far as wording can. I would still want the record to state the omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang openly. I do not need B004 to be uncontroversial; I need it to be the most defensible configuration, and after the round-1 exchange I judge it is.
statement.case_against: The credit boundary remains the real weakness and I do not think wording removes it. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed the HgTe route that Molenkamp's group tested; Zhang is deceased and the other two are outside a three-name cap. Seven of eight round-1 files raise this, which is evidence that the committee sees it, but it does not shrink the gap. A narrow citation makes the omission less visible, not less real. The 2016 prize also leaves a residual risk that the award reads as a second topological prize in ten years. Finally, if the committee gives more weight to demonstrated, deployed measurement capability than to conceptual reach, B006 is the cleaner configuration on attribution and I would not regard that choice as an error.

responses.point: Mr Kroll argues that the lattice clock is not incremental: Katori's magic-wavelength condition broke the trade-off between atom number and systematic shifts, the 2005 prize supplied the counter and the 2012 prize concerned single quantum systems, and a citation anchored on the lattice concept answers the overlap objection.
responses.response: This moved me more than my round-1 text suggested. I called B006 a precision advance within a field honoured in 2005; the many-atom, trap-shift-free architecture is more than that, and I withdraw the word incremental as a description of the concept. I still rank it second because my objection was never only novelty. The credit leakage towards ion-clock and other lattice-clock laboratories that you list yourself, and the fact that the redefinition of the second has not yet happened, leave part of the case prospective. Your disclosure of the Hall-laboratory stay is properly made; I would not treat it as disqualifying but I would want Ms Lindroth's check of Ye's place relative to the comb lineage recorded. If the committee concludes that novelty is established, B006 becomes the strongest alternative, and I would support it over every candidate other than B004.

responses.point: Mr Johansson keeps B004 first but insists that the citation be drawn tightly around the Z2 quantum spin Hall prediction and its first observation, so that three-dimensional work is not drawn in and the 2016 overlap is limited.
responses.response: I adopt your wording and have changed my own citation to match it: the prediction of the time-reversal-invariant topological insulator and the quantum spin Hall effect, and its first observation in HgTe quantum wells. I want to be candid about what this achieves. It excludes Fu, Kane, Mele, Moore, Balents, Hasan and Shen from the claim, which is right, but it does not answer the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang question, and I do not think we should present the narrow wording as a cure. I agree with you that the physics is distinct from the 2016 citation, because the protection comes from time-reversal symmetry and not from a quantised Hall conductance in a field.

responses.point: Mr Mehlig argues that waiting for the pairing mechanism in magic-angle graphene may mean waiting indefinitely, that the discovery can be cited as flat-band correlated physics separately from the mechanism, and that B004's overlap with 2016 is a reason to weigh B009 higher.
responses.response: You answered my maturity point on its own terms: a citation on the predicted flat bands and the observed correlated and superconducting states does not depend on the mechanism, and I concede that. My remaining objection is the experimental half. Jarillo-Herrero alone would carry credit for a discovery made with Cao and others, and no one on the committee has said that is acceptable. That is a gap of the same family as Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, and I cannot hold B004 to a stricter standard than B009. The difference that remains is time: seven to eight years against about twenty. I also disagree gently that the Z2 class is a corollary of the 2016 work. I think it is distinct, but I accept that this is a judgement. I keep B009 as my second alternative.

responses.point: Mr Danielsson moved from B043 to B004, would anchor the citation on the Z2 theory and the first experimental observation, and wants the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang omission stated explicitly in the language of the record.
responses.response: We agree on both points, and on the citation structure. I would add that you and I both moved from our opening first choices, B043 and B002, to B004 after reading the ballots, and that both of us have an instrument-side affinity for the candidates we left. That is a reason to treat our shift as a response to the others' arguments and not as a pull toward the majority. I will not claim a stronger case for B043 than the committee's evidence supports: source identification is still on few objects and the credit sits inside a very large collaboration.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts a Kane-Mele-Molenkamp citation without Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, and whether a record that states the omission openly is enough.
Whether the 2016 prize makes B004 look repetitive, which is a judgement about timing that the supplied text does not settle.
Whether lattice clocks are a distinct concept beyond the 2005 and 2012 prizes; I now lean towards yes but have not verified the priority and uncertainty figures against the supplied evidence.
I rely on prior knowledge for individual roles in the IceCube and ATLAS/CMS efforts, which the supplied files do not verify.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for B004, the preferred candidate, or for B006 and B009, my alternatives. My documented PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and balloon polarimetry work gives me an astroparticle background close to B043 (IceCube), but I have no documented membership of the IceCube collaboration, and B043 is not in my preferred configuration. I continue to record this as a possible bias and not as a formal recusal issue. I take no position on the recusal questions raised by Mr Kroll and Ms Olsson for B006 beyond noting that neither tie is documented as a collaboration.
